content: database/sql pools connections; each new SQLite connection opened with the bare :memory: name gets its own private in-memory database, so a write on one pooled connection is invisible to a read on another (symptom: no such table). Documented by SQLite inmemorydb.html and repeated across Go issue threads. Fixes: (a) SetMaxOpenConns(1) plus SetMaxIdleConns(1), forcing every operation through the single connection that owns the database and matching SQLite single-writer model; (b) file::memory:?cache=shared URI form, letting several connections share one in-memory database within a process (SQLite >= 3.7.13; the unadorned :memory: name never shares). Named memory databases file:name?mode=memory&cache=shared share only with the same name. With a one-connection pool the database lives as long as the pool retains its idle connection; an idle-timeout eviction that closes the last connection deletes it, so keep ConnMaxIdleTime/ConnMaxLifetime at 0 (no eviction) for :memory:.
